correctness.rationale: Proof is complete for m>=3. A wheel orientation is uniquely reconstructed from its rim bits and prescribed rim indegree parities; the local matrix excludes exactly directed triangles, while two constant-rim cases are removed. Every hub-containing directed cycle forces a directed triangle by a spoke-direction switch. An exhaustive constructive parity analysis proves all feasible signatures realized acyclically for even rim length and exactly the nonconstant ones for odd length. The constant even-length cases have exactly two solutions. An actual direct DAG verifier exhausts all 87,360 orientations for 3<=m<=8 and agrees classwise; the unbounded assertion rests on the proof, not the finite computation.

value.rationale: Prescribed indegree-parity acyclic orientations are an actively studied natural problem. A fixed four-state matrix allows the exact cardinality of each of exponentially many parity fibres to be evaluated with only linear arithmetic operations per signature. The exact parity-dependent support criterion and two-realization boundary cases extend beyond an existence check, the generic cycle-space fibre size and the classical total acyclic orientation count. The result applies to a non-cactus infinite family containing overlapping cycles and covers arbitrarily large rims.
